string_concatenation.quote: It prints Sum: 5; The plus adds a and b first, 2 + 3 is 5, and then the 5 is joined to the text
string_concatenation.rule: wrong rule: arithmetic + binds tighter than string-concatenation +. Right rule: Both uses of + have the same precedence and are evaluated left to right, so "s" + a + b joins a and then b as text; only "s" + (a + b) adds them first.

paths.label: held
paths.quote: It prints Sum: 5; The plus adds a and b first, 2 + 3 is 5, and then the 5 is joined to the text
paths.logic: In "s" + a + b, the numbers a and b are added first and their sum is joined to s.
paths.twin_logic: Both uses of + have the same precedence and are evaluated left to right, so "s" + a + b joins a and then b as text; only "s" + (a + b) adds them first.

paths.label: shown
paths.quote: It prints Sum: 5; The plus adds a and b first, 2 + 3 is 5, and then the 5 is joined to the text
paths.logic: Points to LT (left to right, and each + adds or concatenates according to its operands at that moment). Applied unevenly, a student keeps adding numbers after a String has appeared, or concatenates before any String appears (1 + 2 + "x" as "12x"). (here mixing in: "+ with a String turns the whole other side into a string first")

paths.label: shown
paths.logic: Output is the value's characters followed by a line break: println("Hello, "); println("World!"); prints two lines.

paths.label: broken
paths.quote: It prints Sum: 5; The plus adds a and b first, 2 + 3 is 5, and then the 5 is joined to the text
paths.logic: + adds when both operands are numbers and concatenates when either operand is a String, converting the other operand to a String. It is left-associative, so 1 + 2 + "3" is "33" but "1" + 2 + 3 is "123".
